findings.title: Budget load skipped when feature flag enables mid-session
findings.problem: After this change previousBudgetFiltersRef is initialized from live filter values. When isBudgetManagementEnabled is false at mount and later transitions to true with filters unchanged, hasBudgetFiltersChanged evaluates false and Effect 2 returns early without calling loadProjects with budget params. Effect 1 had already run on mount without budget params. The pre-PR hardcoded 'all' ref incidentally produced a false-positive change detection when the stored filter was 'assigned', which triggered a budget-params load; the live-value initialization removed that incidental behavior.
findings.impact: Budget columns remain empty for the session when the feature flag activates after mount with no concurrent filter change. Reachability is uncertain: the code documents that isBudgetManagementEnabled is assumed stable from first render via the App.tsx gate.
findings.recommendation: Track the previous isBudgetManagementEnabled value in a ref (e.g. prevBudgetEnabledRef). In Effect 2, when detecting a false→true transition (isBudgetManagementEnabled && !prevBudgetEnabledRef.current), call loadProjects with budgetQueryParamsRef.current unconditionally before the hasBudgetFiltersChanged guard, then update prevBudgetEnabledRef.
